object_description: large hall part with an attached workroom structure, forming a funnel-shaped break area
geometry_property: timber structure on a solid concrete base
design_condition: the volume is set to respect the existing kindergarten facade and emphasise the visual and access axis, creating an inclined break area that widens in a funnel shape towards the forest edge

positive: The setting respects the kindergarten facade and emphasises the visual and access axis
An inclined break area stretches in a funnel shape and is bordered by terraced break gardens
The new building with the kindergarten forms a play area of high quality of stay
There is a direct connection to the outside space for kindergarten and workrooms
The open space design offers diverse places to move and retreat responding to the site characteristics
The building is accessed via the break area oriented towards the village centre
An inviting canopy at the main entrance supports orientation
The direct secondary entrances from outside are functionally and organisationally advantageous
The floor plans are very convincing and compactly organised
The entrance hall with counter is centrally located between break area, access core and gallery
The workrooms and ancillary rooms form a good functional unit, convincingly arranged and well sized
The gallery offers a view of the village and a visual connection to the hard court
Access to the halls and orientation in the building are very clear and well solved
A wooden structure with prefabricated elements stands on the solid concrete base
The structural grid and high proportion of glass determine the external appearance convincingly and delicately
The jury appreciated the careful handling of the inventory and the high quality of interior and exterior spaces
A well-thought-out project that is also technically and constructively convincing
negative: Facing the main street the building appears powerful with a basement and a closed facade
The excavations for the secondary entrances increase the excess height of the western facade
They also make integration into the natural terrain in the north more difficult
The central lounge area lacks a direct view of the hall and the view
The outdoor equipment room is not optimally located relative to the hard court and is too small
Seating options for sporting events with numerous visitors are missed
The location of the equipment rooms without direct connection to the hall was controversially discussed
Everyday use of bulky gymnastics equipment is questioned due to the narrow support grid
The proportion of glass is very high compared to the other projects
The settlement and volumetrics, particularly in the east, are not considered compatible with the site
The lack of direct connection between entrance area and hall is judged a defect
